verdict.summary: You can build a visible AI email assistant with an External Google OAuth app. A send-only app uses a sensitive scope. An app that reads, drafts, labels, or otherwise accesses Gmail message data uses restricted scopes. Brand review usually takes 2–3 business days. Restricted-scope verification can take several weeks. If restricted Gmail data is stored or sent through your servers, a CASA security assessment is required.
verdict.activeEffort: 2–4 days, mostly to build review materials, public pages, and security controls. CASA adds separate assessment work.
verdict.waitTime: Brand review usually takes 2–3 business days. Restricted-scope verification can take several weeks. CASA assessment timing is not stated in the researched sources.
verdict.mainGate: Restricted Gmail scopes require verification. If your servers store or transmit data obtained through restricted scopes, CASA is required. CASA is Google's recurring security assessment.

recommendation.text: Use an External web application for each customer's Google account. Use Authorization Code flow with offline access. This fits a SaaS agent serving unrelated users.

sources.quote: Apps for use anywhere are configured as External user types in Google Cloud Console.
Set the value to offline if your application needs to refresh access tokens when the user is not present at the browser.

scopeTiers.text: Send emails only. This is the lowest-review Gmail tier for an agent.

sources.quote: Send email on your behalf.
If your app requests sensitive or restricted scopes, you need to complete the verification process unless your app's use qualifies for an exception.

scopeTiers.need: Send a drafted email after the user approves it.

scopeTiers.text: Read email and settings. This requests a restricted permission and needs stricter review.

sources.quote: View your email messages and settings.
These scopes provide wide access to Google user data and require you to go through a scope verification process before you request the scopes from any Google Account.

scopeTiers.need: Read messages to summarize or answer questions.

scopeTiers.text: Read, draft, send, and organize mail. This requests a restricted permission and needs stricter review.

sources.quote: Read, compose, and send emails from your Gmail account.
If you store or transmit restricted scope data on servers, then you need to complete a security assessment.

scopeTiers.need: Create drafts, send mail, and apply labels.

essentials.text: Request access_type=offline. Store refresh tokens securely. Use expires_in instead of assuming an access-token lifetime. Reconnect users when refresh fails.

sources.quote: The refresh token is only returned if your application set the access_type parameter to offline in the initial request
expires_in — The remaining lifetime of the access token in seconds.
When refreshing an access token or using incremental authorization, the token may have expired or has been invalidated.

essentials.text: Add your HTTPS callback URL to the OAuth client. Match protocol, case, and trailing slash exactly.

sources.quote: The value must exactly match one of the authorized redirect URIs for the OAuth 2.0 client
OAuth 2.0 clients for web apps must use redirect URIs and JavaScript origins that are compliant with Google’s validation rules, including using the HTTPS scheme.

essentials.text: Add named testers before publishing. Testing allows 100 users. External Testing refresh tokens normally expire after seven days.

sources.quote: Only users explicitly added to the test user allowlist can access the app (limited to a hard cap of 100 test users).
external apps in Testing status issue refresh tokens that expire after seven days

essentials.text: Budget 1,200,000 quota units per minute per project. Budget 6,000 units per minute for each user and project. messages.send and watch each cost 100 units.

sources.quote: Per minute per project 1,200,000 quota units
Per minute per user per project 6,000 quota units
messages.send 100
watch 100

essentials.text: Standard Gmail API use has no extra cost. Usage below 80,000,000 units per project does not incur charges. Google plans charges above request limits later in 2026.

sources.quote: All standard use of the Gmail API is available at no additional cost.
Usage under this threshold doesn't incur extra charges and your Google Cloud account isn't billed.
Exceeding the quota request limits is planned to incur charges to your Google Cloud billing account later in 2026.

essentials.text: Publish the External app after verification preparation. Unverified sensitive or restricted apps show warnings and have a 100-user cap.

sources.quote: unverified app warnings (Danger UI) will be displayed to users, and a hard cap of 100 total users applies.
Once your app is published to production, click ‘Prepare for Verification’ to proceed to submit your app for verification.

essentials.text: Explain every requested permission. Submit a working end-to-end video. For restricted permissions, upload an unlisted YouTube video showing each permission.

sources.quote: If your app is requesting any sensitive or restricted scopes , you will need to explain how your app will use these scopes.
Provide a video that demonstrates the functionality, the OAuth flow of the app and shows how the scopes are being used.
Upload the video to YouTube Studio and set Visibility as Unlisted.

essentials.text: Encrypt each customer's tokens at rest. Keep the token store off the public internet. Server storage or transfer of restricted Gmail data requires CASA, Google's security assessment.

sources.quote: For server-side applications that store tokens for many users, encrypt them at rest and ensure that your datastore is not publicly accessible to the Internet.
If you store or transmit restricted scope data on servers, then you need to complete a security assessment.
All applications must be revalidated every year.

sources.quote: Your application redirects the user to Google along with the list of requested permissions.
Recommended, offline access will give you both an access and refresh token so that your app can refresh the access token without user interaction.
https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth

requests.label: Refresh the access token

requests.label: Revoke access

detail.text: Create a Google Cloud project. Configure an External audience in OAuth branding. Do not choose Internal unless all users share one Workspace organization.

sources.quote: Internal apps are accessible to all users within the organization without verification.

detail.text: Enable Gmail API in the project. This lets the app access mailboxes and send mail after user consent.

sources.quote: The Gmail API is a RESTful API that lets you access Gmail mailboxes and send mail.

detail.text: Create a server-side web OAuth client in Credentials. Keep its client secret out of source control. Select only the permissions your product needs.

sources.quote: CLIENT_TYPE must be one of: confidential-client , public-client .
Generally, you should choose the most narrowly focused scope possible and avoid requesting scopes that your app doesn't require.
Do not hardcode the credentials, commit them to a code repository or publish them publicly.

detail.text: Add the exact HTTPS callback URL in the OAuth client's authorized redirect URIs. The URL must belong to your organization.

sources.quote: The value must exactly match one of the authorized redirect URIs for the OAuth 2.0 client
OAuth 2.0 clients for web apps must use redirect URIs and JavaScript origins that are compliant with Google’s validation rules, including using the HTTPS scheme.

steps.title: Draft secure callback logic

detail.text: Use this callback outline. Bind state to the signed user session. Reject a callback when state differs.

sources.quote: Before handling an OAuth 2.0 response, confirm that the state received from Google matches the state sent in your authorization request.
The state parameter should be a unique, non-guessable value generated by your application.

detail.text: Add developers and pilot users in OAuth Audience before testing. Testing access is limited to 100 named users.

sources.quote: Only users explicitly added to the test user allowlist can access the app (limited to a hard cap of 100 test users).

detail.text: Test expired consent and revoked access. On disconnect, revoke and permanently delete stored tokens. In External Testing, refresh tokens normally expire after seven days.

sources.quote: Revoke tokens as soon as they are no longer needed and delete them permanently from your systems.
external apps in Testing status issue refresh tokens that expire after seven days

steps.title: Prepare public app materials

detail.text: Publish a public homepage and privacy policy on the same domain. Verify authorized-domain ownership in Google Search Console. Keep consent branding and contacts current.

sources.quote: Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your site's logged-in users.
The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen
Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console.

steps.output: Homepage, privacy policy, verified domains, and contact details

steps.title: Draft review evidence

detail.text: Use this draft as the basis for your justification and reviewer video. Edit it to match actual product behavior before submitting. Scope justification: describe exactly which Gmail data the feature accesses and why each requested scope is needed. State that Gmail data is not used to train a shared model. Video: show the homepage, consent screen, sign-in, the feature using Gmail data, disconnect, deletion, and every requested permission.

sources.quote: Provide a video that demonstrates the functionality, the OAuth flow of the app and shows how the scopes are being used.
Transferring, selling, or using user data to create, train, or improve a machine learning or artificial intelligence model beyond that specific user’s personalized model

steps.output: Scope justification: gmail.readonly reads only user-selected mail for on-screen summaries. No Gmail data trains a shared model. Video: show homepage, consent screen, sign-in, selected message, summary, disconnect, and deletion. Show every requested permission.

detail.text: Publish the app. Select Prepare for Verification. Submit each permission justification and the unlisted demo video. Ensure project owners and editors receive review email.

sources.quote: Once your app is published to production, click ‘Prepare for Verification’ to proceed to submit your app for verification.
All communications with the OAuth review team will occur over email to the project owners and project editors configured when setting up your project.

detail.text: When Google Trust and Safety contacts you, start CASA. CASA is Google's risk-based security assessment. Use a Google-approved independent assessor when required.

sources.quote: the Google Trust and Safety team will contact you when it is time to initiate the security assessment process.
the system must undergo an annual security assessment from an independent, third-party assessor that is approved by Google.

steps.title: Wait for verification

detail.text: Google reviews branding first and then restricted permissions. Respond to review email promptly. CASA timing is not stated in the researched sources.

sources.quote: manual review process that usually takes 2-3 business days
the restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete.

steps.effort: wait: 2–3 business days plus several weeks

detail.text: Enable the approved production connection. Request no permission beyond the verified feature. Show AI output as a user-facing productivity feature.

sources.quote: Applications that enhance the email experience for productivity purposes ... or providing generative AI summaries
Limit your use of data to providing or improving user-facing features that are prominent in the requesting application's user interface

detail.text: Add prompt-injection protections before giving Gmail content to an AI model. Do not create a shared training corpus from Gmail data.

sources.quote: Protecting against prompt injection techniques by either using Google Cloud Platform's Model Armor or other prompt injection protection.
Terms of Service prohibits the scraping, building databases (including databases for model training purposes), or otherwise creating permanent copies of Google User data.

gotchas.text: gmail.modify cannot permanently delete mail without using Trash first.

sources.quote: This scope does not allow immediate, permanent deletion of threads and messages, bypassing the trash.

sources.quote: unverified app warnings (Danger UI) will be displayed to users, and a hard cap of 100 total users applies.
